claims.source_ref: Proposition 1 and Eqs. A19-A23, PDF p. 25
claims.derivation: After transposition, both block products equal L(A tensor I) R(I tensor B*) because left and right regular actions commute; their sum is zero over GF(2).
claims.falsification: The independent cyclic-group instances of orders 3, 5, and 7 all produce an identically zero H_X H_Z^T matrix.

claims.derivation: n=|G|(c1 c2+r1 r2), rank(H_X)<=r1 c2|G|, and rank(H_Z)<=c1 r2|G| imply k>=|G|(c1-r1)(c2-r2).
claims.falsification: The three finite cyclic instances saturate k>=|G| and would fail immediately if either rank bound or block count were mis-normalized.

claims.derivation: Invertible pivot blocks make every kernel vector unique from its free coordinates and every cokernel class unique on free coordinates; the tensor representatives therefore have delta symplectic pairing.
claims.falsification: The independent J150 construction verifies both kernels and the full delta pairing. This supports the conditional theorem, not the inconsistent printed J300 pivot claim.

claims.source_ref: Theorem 6 and Eqs. E1-E13, PDF pp. 50-52
claims.derivation: Theorem 8 supplies the upper bound. Summing the repeated blocks maps every mixed-support X logical to a nonzero B-codeword, while invertibility propagates every mixed-support Z logical through all d_rep pairs, giving the matching lower bounds.
claims.falsification: The d_rep=1 boundary reduces to the base-code bound and the proof explicitly uses pivot invertibility where a singular counterexample could enter.

claims.derivation: The two bridge analyses bound X and Z sectors separately and reduce all four merged-code distances to min(d_rep,d_B); no sector is inferred from resource arithmetic.
claims.falsification: The review checked that the final minimum covers both bridges and both Pauli sectors, ruling out a one-sided distance argument.

claims.source_ref: Theorem 8 and Eqs. G1-G9, PDF pp. 57-60
claims.derivation: A minimum base-code word is placed in one row or column. Full row rank yields a complementary projector ensuring some group translate is outside the stabilizer image while preserving Hamming weight.
claims.falsification: Remark 12's rank-deficient construction is an explicit hypothesis-removal test, so the review retains full row rank as indispensable.

claims.source_ref: Remark 12 and Eqs. G10-G11, PDF p. 60
claims.derivation: The printed matrices have ranks 22 and 23 rather than 24 and classical kernel distances eight; the claimed LP distance ten is logically sufficient to refute removal of the rank hypothesis.
claims.falsification: The terminal campaign independently reproduces ranks 22/23, classical distances 8/8, and [[200,13]] dimensions. Its exact quantum-distance MILP reaches the frozen time limit without a lower-bound certificate, so the distance-ten subclaim remains an evidenced capability failure.

claims.source_ref: Proposition 4 and Eq. G16, PDF p. 62
claims.derivation: Normality of the commutator subgroup makes its group sum commute with every group element; swapping two weighted coordinates therefore constructs an explicit kernel word with the stated support bound.
claims.falsification: For an abelian group the commutator subgroup is trivial, reducing the expression to the expected two-entry kernel construction.

claims.source_ref: Theorem 9 and Eqs. G17-G18, PDF p. 63
claims.derivation: The orbit sum r=1+g+...+g^(ord(g)-1) is annihilated by 1+g over GF(2) and has weight at most ord(g), producing a base-code word and hence the quantum upper bound under Theorem 8.
claims.falsification: The g=e limit gives the zero ring entry rather than a nonzero codeword, making the nontrivial-entry hypothesis explicit.

claims.source_ref: Theorem 13 and Eqs. G29-G35, PDF pp. 65-67
claims.derivation: The proof exhausts all admissible two-row four-column weight partitions with row sum at most six and column sum at most three; each connected case has permanent bound at most 14 and the remaining disconnected case reduces to a 1x2 bound of six.
claims.falsification: The listed partitions of total weight 12 exhaust ordered parts in {0,1,2,3} up to permutation; recomputing their triplet sums reproduces maxima 14,14,12,12,18 and isolates the disconnected exception.

claims.source_ref: Algorithm 1 and Eqs. H4-H8, PDF pp. 68-69
claims.derivation: Sampling null-space basis rows and applying invertible row operations preserves the null-space span; undoing the column permutation restores the original coordinates, and the opposite-nullspace test excludes stabilizers.
claims.falsification: The independent implementation recovers distance three on the Steane CSS code and rejects zero/stabilizer rows.

claims.derivation: Inclusion-exclusion over the required basis rows yields the exact sketch-containment probability; independent trials amplify it as 1-(1-p)^N.
claims.falsification: The implementation checks zero-row, full-coverage, monotonic-sketch-size, and probability-range limits.

claims.derivation: Under the paper's uniform full-rank pivot-set model, the required pivots occur with a hypergeometric ratio; multiplication by sketch inclusion and independent-trial amplification gives H13.
claims.falsification: A 20,000-sample seeded Monte Carlo agrees with the exact pivot-set probability within 0.02; the result is explicitly conditional on uniform pivots.

claims.derivation: Composing the inverse of the current regular permutation with the next gives L(g_j^-1 g_i) and R(g_j^-1 g_i) under the stated action conventions.
claims.falsification: Exact permutation matrices over C7 satisfy both identities for nonidentity g_i=5 and g_j=2.

claims.source_ref: Proposition 5 and Eqs. J4-J7, PDF p. 87
claims.derivation: Every bipartite planar layer has at most 2(V-2) edges by Euler's formula and girth at least four; dividing total Tanner edges by this capacity gives J4 and substitution gives J5.
claims.falsification: The independent K3,3 check returns thickness lower bound two, catching the common erroneous 3(V-2) planar-edge normalization.

claims.derivation: At rate 1/5, check weight nine, and n>=150, J5 gives the lower bound three. Partitioning each ring entry by its three monomials yields three layers, each a disjoint union of |G| 3x3 grids because left and right actions commute around every face.
claims.falsification: The upper construction and lower Euler bound are independent; equality would fail if any ring entry repeated a monomial or if a layer face had inconsistent left/right labeling.

claims.derivation: Rayleigh-Ritz with unit norm, centering, and mutual orthogonality selects Laplacian eigenvectors u2 and u3; the Hungarian step then minimizes squared displacement to distinct grid sites.
claims.falsification: The independent four-node cycle exhausts all 24 assignments after eigendecomposition and reaches the minimum assignment cost.
